title: House Robber
description:
Houses are arranged on a straight street, and nums[i] is the amount available at house i. Choose houses to maximize the total collected, under the rule that no two chosen houses share an edge. Return the maximum total as an integer. You may choose no house, so an empty street yields zero; taking a house does not change the values of other houses.

For each prefix of the street, the best total either skips the final house and keeps the previous prefix's best, or takes that house after skipping its immediate predecessor. Carrying those two alternatives forward avoids revisiting the same subsets. A locally richest house is not necessarily part of a globally best choice: two less valuable houses on either side might together be worth more.

The street is a line, not a ring; the first and last houses do not count as neighbors unless there are only two houses. Values are nonnegative, so choosing nothing remains a legal zero-value solution. Return only the optimal amount, not the addresses of the houses. A one-house street returns that house's amount, including when the amount is zero.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [2,7,9,3,1]
Output: 12

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,1,1,2]
Output: 4

Example 3:

Input: nums = []
Output: 0

Constraints:

  • 0 <= nums.length <= 100
  • 0 <= nums[i] <= 10,000
  • Adjacent indices cannot both be selected.
